## Getting started

1. Clone the repo and install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), then `uv sync --group dev`
2. Create your `.env` from the template: `cp .env.example .env`. It is gitignored; never commit it or paste keys in chat.
3. Put the keys into `.env`:

   | Variable | Where to get it | Needed for |
   |---|---|---|
   | `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN` | Portal → Settings → API token | Everything (download, poll, watch) |
   | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | [Claude Console](https://console.anthropic.com/) → API keys | `analyze` and `watch` with the default Claude backend |
   | `ASK_LLM_PROVIDER` + `ASK_LLM_API_KEY` | OpenAI key, or empty for a local llama.cpp server | Only if you use another backend (see below) |

   `SOONY_PORTAL_URL` is already filled in by the template.
4. Set up Entire so your agent sessions are tracked: see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#entire-session-tracking)

### Download the portal data once

Needs only `SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN`, no LLM key:

```bash
uv run ask-soony download              # all current files into data/portal/, under their portal paths
uv run ask-soony download some/folder  # or into another folder
```

Run it again any time to bring the folder up to date: only new or changed files are fetched (the first run uses `archive.zip`). Files removed from the portal stay in the folder. Every version also lands in the version store (`data/store/`, see below). All of `data/` is gitignored: the data is confidential.

input.new_string:
### Dashboard: what changed, when

Every new or changed file version gets a "what changed" summary without any LLM: CSV files are compared row by row (rows added, removed, changed with old → new values; columns added, removed or renamed), Excel files cell by cell, everything else as a text diff. The dashboard shows each poll with its changes, every file's version history with diffs, the agent's findings and the supplier mail log (`data/outbox/`, `data/inbox/`).

```bash
uv run ask-soony serve --interval 300   # poll every 5 min + dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8765
uv run ask-soony dashboard              # dashboard only
```

Set `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` in `.env` (HTTP basic auth, any user name). The dashboard listens on localhost only and refuses other addresses without a password. To share it, put a tunnel in front, for example a Cloudflare Tunnel with its own config file:

```yaml
# ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml
protocol: http2            # QUIC is often blocked on event and campus networks
tunnel: <tunnel id>
credentials-file: /path/to/<tunnel id>.json
ingress:
  - hostname: ask-soony.example.com   # one level below the zone, so the free certificate covers it
    service: http://localhost:8765
  - service: http_status:404
```

```bash
cloudflared tunnel create ask-soony
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml route dns <tunnel id> ask-soony.example.com
cloudflared tunnel --config ~/.cloudflared/ask-soony.yml run
```

Pass `--config` to `route dns` too: without it, `cloudflared` takes the tunnel from the default `config.yml` and may attach the hostname to a different tunnel.

The dashboard is up and refreshes every 5 minutes. It runs on your Mac and is reachable from outside through a Cloudflare tunnel. You chose the Mac over ada.

**Where:** https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev
- Password: `ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD` in `.env`, with any user name. I generated it and haven't shown it here.
- Without the password the dashboard returns 401. I checked that and the logged-in page from outside.

**What it shows:**
- **Changes:** each poll with its new, changed and removed files, and a "what changed" summary per version, without AI. Examples from the drops:
  - `products.csv`: "columns renamed: plan_weekly_units → weekly_plan_qty; columns added: day_one_qty, valid_from"
  - the export-control news: "China tightens export licensing for rare-earth magnets…"
- **Per file:** version history, the diff to the previous version, and a download.
- **Findings** (once the agent runs with an API key) and **Supplier mail**: all sent and received mails.

**What's running** (in `tmux`):
- `ask-soony-serve`: polls every 5 minutes plus the dashboard. It runs under `caffeinate`, so the Mac doesn't fall asleep; closing the lid still stops it.
- `ask-soony-tunnel`: the tunnel over HTTP/2, because QUIC is blocked on this network.
- Logs in `data/logs/`. Stop with `tmux kill-session -t ask-soony-serve` and `tmux kill-session -t ask-soony-tunnel`.

**Two fixes during setup:**
- My first DNS entry landed on your old `lampy-dev` tunnel. It was never reachable that way, and I fixed it right away.
- `soony.agents.stenglein.dev` got no certificate, because the free certificate only covers one subdomain level. So the address is now `ask-soony.stenglein.dev`, and I deleted the old record.

**Your other questions:**
- **Mail test without the thread:** Boise's agent **doesn't remember across threads.** In the new thread it claimed the cards were still on hold and our EXW confirmation was missing, although it had confirmed the release 15 minutes earlier. Our product has to track the status per supplier itself and answer in the right thread.
- **Structured updates:** Boise chose **option (b), a fixed email format**, and is looking for a contact for API or EDI.
- **New drop at 17:20:** China is tightening export licences for magnets. PackRight's Collector's boxes from December will be about 6 weeks late, and there's no second source. **The launch isn't affected**: November is covered.

**Commits:** three new local commits on `main` (`0345691` change summaries, `6af4e33` dashboard, `d7d6e45` JSON summaries). Tests (7 of 7) and lint pass. **Not pushed yet**, waiting for your OK.

content.text:
Here's the proposal. Each field exists because of a problem we actually ran into today.

**Format: "Soony supplier status v1"**: a plain text block in the email body (no attachment), semicolons, one line per order line, header line first. The supplier can type it by hand or export it from their system.

```
#SOONY-STATUS v1
PO;ITEM;SOONY_PART;SUPPLIER_PART;REV;QTY_ORDERED;QTY_CONFIRMED;QTY_SHIPPED;UNIT_PRICE;CURRENCY;INCOTERM;CONFIRMED_DATE;STATUS;HOLD_REASON;MODE;AWB_OR_CONTAINER;DELIVERY_NOTE;ETD;ETA;NOTE
4500318769;00010;CMP-GAM-002;;;5500;5500;5500;6.11;USD;EXW Boise;2026-11-26;SHIPPED;;AIR;020-94727021;;2026-11-19;2026-11-21;
4500318769;00020;CMP-GAM-001;;;36000;36000;0;10.93;USD;EXW Boise;2026-11-23;ON_HOLD;INCOTERM_CONFIRMATION;AIR;020-48113304;;;;awaiting written EXW confirmation
#END
```

**Required:** `PO`, `ITEM`, `SOONY_PART`, `QTY_CONFIRMED`, `CONFIRMED_DATE`, `STATUS`. Everything else when known.

**Why each field, from today's data:**

| Field | Problem it catches |
|---|---|
| `QTY_CONFIRMED` + `QTY_SHIPPED` | Hwaseong flew only 28,000 of 48,000, which we only learned from free text |
| `STATUS` + `HOLD_REASON` | Boise "on hold", our shipment list said "booked" |
| `INCOTERM` + `UNIT_PRICE` + `CURRENCY` | DDP vs EXW at Boise; price differences between order confirmations and SAP |
| `SUPPLIER_PART` | PackRight uses its own numbers (PR-SL-0604 etc.), so the mapping travels with every line |
| `REV` (artwork revision) | Sleeves revision B vs C. Since ECN-118, revision B must not be packed |
| `DELIVERY_NOTE` | The art book receipt booked 80,000 vs 8,000; the note number lets us check it against the scan |
| `AWB_OR_CONTAINER` + `ETD` + `ETA` | Status per shipment, instead of the shipment spreadsheet "updated when someone remembers" |

**Allowed status values:** `CONFIRMED`, `CHANGED`, `PACKED`, `ON_HOLD`, `RELEASED`, `SHIPPED`, `PARTIAL`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`. Hold reasons from a short list: `INCOTERM_CONFIRMATION`, `QUALITY`, `CAPACITY`, `EXPORT_LICENCE`, `PAYMENT`, `OTHER`.

**Notices that aren't tied to one order line,** as separate lines in the same block:
```
#NOTICE;TYPE;EFFECTIVE_FROM;EFFECTIVE_TO;AFFECTED_PARTS;TEXT
#NOTICE;CAPACITY;2026-11-21T14:00+01:00;2026-11-23T06:00+01:00;CMP-GAM-008;bindery maintenance, finished goods can ship
```
Types: `CAPACITY` (Nowak's downtime), `EXPORT` (PackRight's magnet licence), `PRICE` (price lists), `ARTWORK`, `QUALITY`.

**Rules that make it machine-readable:**
- Dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`, times with timezone.
- Quantities without thousand separators: the launch status had "640.000", German formatting.
- Decimal point, not comma: the old SAP export has `1,5200`.
- **Bank detail changes never through this format.** Only in writing plus a phone call. That's against payment fraud, the example from the organizers' briefing.

Boise wanted the template **to her**, and **the EXW confirmation repeated in her thread**. I'd send both in one reply: the confirmation in the same words as before (no new decision), plus the template with her two order lines as an example, as above.

Should I send it like that? And should I also save the format as a spec in the repo (`docs/supplier-status-format.md`, with invented example values) so our watcher can read it later?
yes, send it

# Supplier status format v1

A plain text block that suppliers put into the body of an email whenever something changes on an order: a confirmation, a date or quantity change, a hold or release, a dispatch. Our watcher reads it from the inbox, so status no longer has to be pieced together from PDFs and free text. Suppliers can type it by hand or export it from their system; it needs no portal and no integration project.

## Order lines

One line per PO item, fields separated by semicolons, header line first:

```
#SOONY-STATUS v1
PO;ITEM;SOONY_PART;SUPPLIER_PART;REV;QTY_ORDERED;QTY_CONFIRMED;QTY_SHIPPED;UNIT_PRICE;CURRENCY;INCOTERM;CONFIRMED_DATE;STATUS;HOLD_REASON;MODE;AWB_OR_CONTAINER;DELIVERY_NOTE;ETD;ETA;NOTE
4500000001;00010;CMP-XYZ-001;SUP-PN-17;C;10000;10000;6000;1.25;USD;EXW Example City;2026-01-15;PARTIAL;;AIR;000-12345678;DN-260110-001;2026-01-10;2026-01-12;balance of 4000 on next flight
4500000001;00020;CMP-XYZ-002;;;5000;5000;0;0.80;USD;EXW Example City;2026-01-20;ON_HOLD;INCOTERM_CONFIRMATION;;;;;;awaiting written confirmation
#END
```

Required: `PO`, `ITEM`, `SOONY_PART`, `QTY_CONFIRMED`, `CONFIRMED_DATE`, `STATUS`. All other fields when known.

| Field | Why it is there |
|---|---|
| `QTY_CONFIRMED`, `QTY_SHIPPED` | Partial shipments show up as numbers, not in a sentence |
| `STATUS`, `HOLD_REASON` | A hold at the supplier is visible even when a booking exists |
| `INCOTERM`, `UNIT_PRICE`, `CURRENCY` | Term and price mismatches with our PO surface on the first message |
| `SUPPLIER_PART` | Suppliers using their own part numbers map to ours on every line |
| `REV` | Artwork or drawing revision, so superseded revisions are caught before packing |
| `DELIVERY_NOTE` | Lets receiving match a booked quantity to the paper delivery note |
| `MODE`, `AWB_OR_CONTAINER`, `ETD`, `ETA` | Shipment status per order line instead of a manually kept tracker |

`STATUS`: `CONFIRMED`, `CHANGED`, `PACKED`, `ON_HOLD`, `RELEASED`, `SHIPPED`, `PARTIAL`, `DELIVERED`, `CANCELLED`

`HOLD_REASON`: `INCOTERM_CONFIRMATION`, `QUALITY`, `CAPACITY`, `EXPORT_LICENCE`, `PAYMENT`, `OTHER`

## Notices

Events that are not tied to one PO item go into the same block:

```
#NOTICE;TYPE;EFFECTIVE_FROM;EFFECTIVE_TO;AFFECTED_PARTS;TEXT
#NOTICE;CAPACITY;2026-01-21T14:00+01:00;2026-01-23T06:00+01:00;CMP-XYZ-008;line maintenance, finished goods can still ship
```

`TYPE`: `CAPACITY`, `EXPORT`, `PRICE`, `ARTWORK`, `QUALITY`

## Conventions

- Dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`, times with time zone offset
- Quantities without thousand separators; decimal point for prices
- Bank detail changes are never accepted through this format: only in writing plus a confirming phone call

what is erp vs sap?

**ERP** is the *category* of software and **SAP** is a *product*, the best-known one in that category:

- **ERP** ("Enterprise Resource Planning") is the central business software of a company: purchasing, warehouse, production, sales, accounting, all in one system with one database. Orders, goods receipts, stock and invoices are recorded there.
- **SAP** is a German software company and its ERP system of the same name (today mostly "SAP S/4HANA", previously "SAP ECC"). It's the market leader among large companies. Other ERP systems are Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, or Odoo for smaller firms.

At Soony:
- The portal folder is called `soony/erp/`, the generic term, and the onboarding notes say "SAP holds the purchase orders, nothing else". So Soony's ERP *is* SAP.
- You can tell from the data: the old order export has German SAP field names (`EBELN` = PO number, `MENGE` = quantity, `WEDAT` = goods receipt date). The new supplier profiles even name the SAP transaction they came from ("SAP XK03 extract", the screen for displaying a supplier record).
- What's *not* in SAP at Soony is exactly what keeps causing trouble: the shipment list (Excel), order confirmations (PDF), delivery notes (scans) and contracts. Hence "only 2 of 7 steps have a system" in the slides.

For the pitch: our product doesn't replace the ERP. It works **next to** it and connects SAP to all the paper and email. That's also why it works for other customers, whether they use SAP, Oracle or something else.

The Excel tracker is the manual spreadsheet "updated when someone remembers". The ERP list is a system export from Friday. They differ mostly in **what's missing**, and both lag behind reality.

**1. The tracker has only 14 of 25 shipments, and exactly the launch-critical ones are missing.**
It contains only sea containers already underway. Missing are all 11 shipments that are by air, by road, or still "booked":

| Missing from the tracker | What | ETA | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| SHP-04311 Hwaseong, air | GH6 game cards | 21 Nov | The 48,000 cards, of which only 28,000 flew |
| SHP-04313 Karton Nowak, road | Sleeves (rev C) | 21 Nov | The 20,000 valid sleeves arriving tonight |
| SHP-04314 Boise, air | GH6 game cards | 23 Nov | The 36,000 Boise had on hold |
| SHP-04310 Boise, air | GH5 cards | 21 Nov | Already underway |
| SHP-04316 Karton Nowak, road | GH5 sleeves | 22 Nov | |
| 6 more | Sea and air from late Nov to Jan | | After the launch |

If Soony plans from the tracker, it doesn't see the inbound deliveries that decide Sunday.

**2. Where both have the same shipment, the tracker is behind:**
- **SHP-04276 (PackRight, 350,000 card cases):** ERP says **arrived at the Hamburg port**, tracker still says "in transit" with the note "RP: call terminal". Exactly the container we need to pick up for the 32,000 missing cases.
- **SHP-04281 (Hwaseong, GH5 cards):** ERP "in delivery", tracker "in transit".
- Everything else (ETAs, waybills, POs) matches.

**3. Even the ERP list is out of date.** Its newest entry is from **Fri 20 Nov, 17:00**. We know more from the supplier mails:
- **SHP-04311:** ERP "booked". In reality **only 28,000 of 48,000** flew (Hwaseong's shipping advice); the remaining 20,000 come on 24 Nov.
- **SHP-04314:** ERP "booked". Boise had it **on hold** until our EXW confirmation and has now released it, with Frankfurt on 23 Nov.
- **Neither list contains quantities.** You can only see from other files (launch plan, shipping advice) how much is in a shipment, so partial shipments are invisible in both.

**In short:** the tracker shows 14 of 25 shipments and is out of date; the ERP export is complete but a day old and has no quantities; the true status is in the supplier mails. This is exactly the gap our product should close: supplier status in the agreed format (the way Boise just sent it) updates every shipment line automatically, and the dashboard shows where ERP, tracker and supplier disagree.

Yes, your notes resolve it. The key line is **"File in portal is SAP export"**, together with **"Technician type stuff manually in sap"**.

**The answer:**
- **Everything in `erp/` comes from SAP:** orders, goods receipts, stock, the shipment list and the pack-out log.
- **But only ordering and packing *originate* in a system.** Everything else reaches SAP because someone **types it in by hand** from emails, PDFs and paper ("Have to input all data by hand", "Mostly from internal or forwarded").
- So the slide is right: "2 of 7 steps have a system" means only two steps produce their data in a system. The rest is in SAP, but only as a **manual copy** with typos and delays.

**That explains the contradictions we found:**

| What we saw | Explanation from your notes |
|---|---|
| Art book receipt 80,000 instead of 8,000 | Typed by hand from the delivery note ("human errors, put wrong stuff") |
| ERP shipment list last updated Fri 17:00, Boise hold missing | Entered by hand when someone gets to it ("Wrong information months later") |
| Excel tracker next to the SAP list, both different | "Different people have different preferred ways", "spreadsheets and random PDFs flying around" |
| PO says DDP, contract says EXW | Typed in wrong when ordering; nobody checks against the contract |

**And they give us product requirements, straight from the customer:**
1. **SAP should stay the single source of truth** ("If SAP is single source of truth that would be great"). So we're no new system next to SAP, but the layer that gets data from email, PDF and supplier format **checked into SAP**.
2. **Get rid of the manual typing** ("eliminate human errors"). This is where the agreed supplier format comes in: Boise sent its status line today, and the system can take it over without retyping.
3. **Only flag what's uncertain or big** ("If system unsure or big one then would like to know it but generally rely on it"). That's the rule for when a person has to approve. Small, safe updates go through automatically.
4. **Trust per supplier** ("Can trust different suppliers differently?"): Boise's structured status gets more trust than a scan; a supplier with frequent mismatches gets checked more strictly.
5. **Two-way SAP connection** ("bidirectional"): reading is the base, writing back (for example corrected delivery terms or confirmed dates) is the goal.
6. **Being able to trust the data fully:** every value shows its source and when it was last confirmed.

**For the pitch:** "Soony's IT lead told us: 'We want to fully trust our data. If SAP is the single source of truth, that would be great.' So we don't build another dashboard next to SAP. We make what lands in SAP correct."

I've read both transcripts in full. Some things in them aren't in your notes, and some are better quotes.

**What's in the transcripts beyond your notes:**

*Senior Buyer (Felix):*
- **The core requirement, as a usable quote:** *"Your tool has to tell me, before the supplier does, that something will not arrive. Otherwise I would not use it."* Not with 100% accuracy, *"but that you at least try to take action if you see some signals."*
- **Transparency alone isn't enough:** *"It solves the problem of transparency, but in the end if it doesn't arrive [the problem remains]."* The tool has to offer alternatives too.
- **Why autonomy matters, not just human-in-the-loop:** if every approval waits, *"it will take ages because they don't look into the notifications"*. For the demo: *"stop at some point… the human can decide or not, but it should be able to run autonomously."*
- **Approval chains are different in every company,** and *"this is what we actually do, building up those approval chains"*, meaning Lio itself. So make them configurable, not hardcoded.
- **Out of role:** emails **don't change the portal data.** You *"get the data… work with it locally… update it based on what you sent them via mail"*. That answers our earlier question: the portal data is the same for everyone, and the replies are additional information. Too many mails can mean they stop replying.
- **Scope:** *"Don't build 12 fancy features"*, but the whole process (order → track → arrival) should work. Product sense and generalisability matter more than deep data knowledge.

*IT (Nils):*
- **Most annoying task:** mailbox → new receipt or confirmation → **typing it into SAP by hand** (often the intern). The team said it themselves in the interview: *"If you just automate that… that would be a very easy project."*
- **Wrong supplier documents get reclaimed, and finance takes over.** So we shouldn't "correct" documents ourselves, only flag them and trigger the reclaim.
- **Errors surface weeks or months later,** and then someone debugs and fixes the database or the contract.
- **"Emails for now would already help,"** but they also want something for the future. A two-way SAP connection is "out of scope for the weekend".
- **Out of role on thread memory:** it's *"part of the thread"*, the way it's technically set up, not a deliberate scenario element. So it's a technical limit, not something to build the pitch on.
- **Out of role:** confusion at the start is intended, and *"we didn't want everyone to build the same thing"*. Your team also mentions its own direction at the end: **"build the verifier first", then "an easier input method"**.

**What this means for our product:**
1. **Early warning before the supplier speaks up:** watch signals like status lists not updating, partial shipments, holds, downtime notices and export news, and warn as soon as a delivery for the launch is at risk. Felix calls exactly this the reason to buy.
2. **Always attach an action to a warning:** for example the Nowak art books, sorting the statue lot, or Collector's first for the game cards. Not just "red light".
3. **Verifier before SAP:** check everything coming in (supplier format, PDFs, scans) against PO, contract and receipt, and only push it into SAP when it's consistent. That's Nils's "SAP as the single source of truth".
4. **Human approval with an autonomy switch:** escalation rules configurable per company (cost, critical to the launch, supplier switch).
5. **Generalisable:** nothing about Soony in the code. The demo shows it on Soony's data.

The doc is up to date: https://claude.ai/artifact/5A9jFV1dXSg1zdCZaFACp6. Right after the summary there are now two new sections:
- **"Update Sat 17:30":** the three new drops, the CPO rules, the new position table and the Boise outcome.
- **"What Soony's team told us":** the key quotes from Felix and Nils, and what they mean for the product.

**Is the core idea right: compare SAP with order confirmations, then with scanned receipts, and update along the way?** Yes, that's the right core. In procurement it's called a **three-way match**: order, confirmation and receipt must agree. The data provides an example for every comparison:

| Comparison | Documents | Found in the data |
|---|---|---|
| **Order ↔ confirmation** | SAP PO line vs supplier's PDF or mail | Boise: DDP vs EXW; price differences; PackRight confirms artwork revision B |
| **Order ↔ contract** | PO terms vs contract or price list | Delivery terms and prices that contradict the contract |
| **Confirmation ↔ dispatch** | Confirmed vs actually shipped quantity | Hwaseong: 48,000 confirmed, only 28,000 flown |
| **Receipt ↔ scan** | Receipt booked in SAP vs delivery note scan | Art books: 80,000 booked, 8,000 on the note |
| **Receipt ↔ quality** | Stock "usable" vs inspection report | 5,600 statues failed inspection but are booked as usable |

**"Update along the way"** means each order line has a timeline (ordered → confirmed → shipped → received → usable), and every new document advances it or produces a contradiction. Our watcher and the mail inbox already deliver those documents; the comparison step is what's missing.

**On leaving out shipping:** I'd leave out *tracking* (ships, GPS, carriers), but keep **one field: when it will arrive.** Felix's buying criterion is "tell me before the supplier does that something will not arrive". That only works if the verifier compares the latest promised date (from confirmation, supplier status or the shipment export) with when the part is needed. One date comparison, no tracking system, and that's the demo's money shot.

**Demo or UI first? I'd start with a short demo script** (about 15 minutes): what the jury sees in the 3 minutes, in 4 or 5 beats. For example:
1. Plan says "all ok".
2. A new drop arrives, and the verifier catches the art book receipt against the scan.
3. Warning before the supplier: Collector's short by 5,900.
4. Action card: order from Nowak, approved with one click (or autonomous).
5. Reply in the thread, status turns green.

**The UI follows from that:** essentially one screen with the order lines and their timeline traffic lights, the contradictions with sources side by side, and an action card with approve or autonomous mode. We build only what the script needs, which matches Felix's "no 12 features".

Should I write the demo script and a rough UI sketch next, as a new section in the doc, so the team can agree on them?
Could we give people an automated call if sth is critical wrong that threatens the launch? What services are there for this?

Yes. Felix said himself: "Ship game as main goal… could also call someone if critical". An automated call for **launch-threatening** issues fits our escalation rules well. The options, by effort:

| Option | How it works | Effort | Good for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Telephony API with text-to-speech:** Twilio Programmable Voice (alternatives Vonage, Plivo, Sinch, Telnyx) | One API call places the call and reads a text aloud. With "Press 1 to approve, 2 to escalate" the answer comes back to our server | About 1 h, plus account and phone number | **Approval by phone:** the call *is* the approval step |
| **AI voice agent:** Vapi, Retell AI, Bland AI, ElevenLabs Conversational AI (usually on Twilio underneath) | An AI talks freely: explains the problem, answers questions ("What does the order cost?"), takes the decision | 2–3 h, more fragile | Wow effect in the demo, but more can go wrong live |
| **On-call tools:** PagerDuty, incident.io, Better Stack | Built for IT outages: call, SMS, app, escalation chain until someone confirms | About 30 min setup, no custom call text logic | Escalation chains ("no answer in 5 minutes, call the boss") without building them |
| **Push with emergency priority:** Pushover "Emergency" | Repeats loudly until confirmed, even in silent mode | 15 min | Cheap fallback, but not a real call |

My recommendation for the demo: **Twilio with text-to-speech and keypad input**, wired to our existing rules:
- Only on **"critical"** (threatens the launch) and when nobody reacts in the dashboard or app within X minutes.
- The call reads one specific sentence, e.g. *"Collector's Edition at risk: 5,900 art books missing. Karton Nowak offers 8,000 from stock for 16,800 euros. Press 1 to order, 2 to escalate to the Head of Procurement."*
- Pressing 1 triggers the same approval as the click in the dashboard. No answer means the next person in the escalation chain.
- On stage: a teammate's phone rings live. That's very memorable and fits "the moment a human has to decide".

**What to know beforehand:**
- **Twilio trial accounts** can only call **pre-verified numbers**, and each call starts with a trial notice. That's fine for the demo with our own phones; for clean calls you'd need a few euros of credit.
- **A German number** at Twilio needs a regulatory process. A US number is quicker and can call German phones too.
- **Only call our own team,** never real people from the data.
- I'm going from my knowledge of these services; I haven't checked current prices and terms. I'd do that before signing up.

Should I build it with Twilio? I'd need someone to create a Twilio account (with a credit card for credit, or trial with verified numbers) and put the account SID, auth token and phone number in `.env`. Or should we first finish the core (verifier plus demo script) and treat the call as a bonus?

---

## Summary

**The idea.** A layer on top of Soony's procurement process that finds what threatens the launch deadline and alerts the right person: a phone call if it is critical, otherwise an email or a notification in the portal.

**Two error sources to tackle:**
1. **Three-way match** (main focus): compare the purchase order in SAP, the supplier's order confirmation (PDF, in its own language) and what Hamburg actually received (scanned delivery note, sometimes with handwritten corrections like "100" crossed out, "80" written over it).
2. **Shipment tracking and prediction:** predict whether a shipment arrives in time, using past patterns, the shipment data and news drops (weather, strikes, etc.), and propose alternatives when it won't (e.g. "this supplier can only deliver 500 of 1,000, here's a draft mail to another supplier, click send").

**Criticality.** For every problem: can it wait two or three hours (notification), or must someone act now (call)? The deadline per order comes from the promised date the buyer enters with the PO.

**Automation and trust.** Start by asking a human; let them allow an action "this time" or "always" (like a permissions prompt). Internal actions can be automatic sooner; anything sent to suppliers gets stricter rules.

**Boundaries agreed:**
- We work for Soony (the buyer). We don't do the procurement, we watch the process and catch problems before they hit the launch.
- We only touch Soony's side ("the upper part"). Suppliers and logistics are out of reach except by email.
- Suppliers refuse to use our system or share tracking data; the most they accept is replying by email in a structured format.
- SAP only has the order and the pack-out data; everything in between (confirmations, tracking sheet, receipts) is email, PDFs, scans and a hand-kept Excel sheet.
- We are not a second SAP: it is a connector or plugin to Soony's SAP.

**Split of work (first part of the call):**
- S0: alert agent (email, phone call via ElevenLabs), then notifications.
- One person: prediction model.
- One person: verification (three-way match).
- S1: dashboard and bringing the pieces together.
- Newcomer: storyline for the pitch, maybe the "our PS5 didn't arrive in time" angle.

**Open questions at the end:**
- How do tracking updates and receiving notes get into the ERP data, and how often? If they are near real time, they can feed the prediction; if they only arrive at the end, they can't.

"""
Alerts: turn a problem found by another module (verification, prediction, the watcher) into the
right notification for the right person, and escalate until someone decides.

- Criticality: a producer may set the severity; with a deadline the module also derives it
  (little time left on something that hits the launch = critical).
- Routing: an escalation policy (JSON, kept out of git because it holds phone numbers) says which
  channels each severity uses, who is called in which order and how long to wait for an answer.
- Decisions: a person approves, rejects or escalates through the dashboard, a phone keypad
  (Twilio) or a voice agent (ElevenLabs). Every step is logged per alert.

Nothing here knows about the customer's parts or suppliers: alerts carry their own text.
"""

import json
import secrets
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from ask_soony.store import SEVERITIES, Store, now_iso

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alerts (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    source TEXT NOT NULL,            -- verification | prediction | watcher | manual
    severity TEXT NOT NULL,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    message TEXT NOT NULL,           -- what is wrong, in one or two sentences
    action TEXT NOT NULL,            -- what we propose to do about it
    deadline TEXT,                   -- when it becomes a problem (ISO 8601)
    impact TEXT NOT NULL,            -- launch | cost | data
    external INTEGER NOT NULL,       -- 1 if the action goes to a supplier
    status TEXT NOT NULL,            -- open | notified | approved | rejected | escalated | resolved
    decision_by TEXT,
    decision_at TEXT,
    token TEXT NOT NULL,             -- secret for decision links and call webhooks
    chain_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    next_escalation_at TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alert_events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    alert_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES alerts(id),
    at TEXT NOT NULL,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,              -- notified | call | decision | escalated | error
    channel TEXT NOT NULL,
    contact TEXT NOT NULL,
    detail TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""

DEFAULT_POLICY = {
    "dashboard_url": "",
    "critical_hours": 24,
    "contacts": [],
    "routes": {
        "critical": {"channels": ["dashboard", "email", "call"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 10},
        "high": {"channels": ["dashboard", "email"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 120},
        "medium": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 0},
        "low": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 0},
        "info": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 0},
    },
}

DECISIONS = {"approve": "approved", "reject": "rejected", "escalate": "escalated", "resolve": "resolved"}


@dataclass
class Contact:
    id: str
    name: str
    role: str
    phone: str = ""
    email: str = ""


@dataclass
class Policy:
    dashboard_url: str = ""
    critical_hours: float = 24
    contacts: list[Contact] = field(default_factory=list)
    routes: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: dict(DEFAULT_POLICY["routes"]))

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "Policy":
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
        data = {**DEFAULT_POLICY, **raw}
        routes = {**DEFAULT_POLICY["routes"], **raw.get("routes", {})}
        return cls(
            dashboard_url=data.get("dashboard_url", "").rstrip("/"),
            critical_hours=float(data.get("critical_hours", 24)),
            contacts=[Contact(**c) for c in data.get("contacts", [])],
            routes=routes,
        )

    def contact(self, contact_id: str) -> Contact | None:
        return next((c for c in self.contacts if c.id == contact_id), None)

    def route(self, severity: str) -> dict:
        return self.routes.get(severity) or self.routes["info"]


@dataclass
class Alert:
    id: int
    created_at: str
    source: str
    severity: str
    title: str
    message: str
    action: str
    deadline: str | None
    impact: str
    external: bool
    status: str
    token: str
    chain_index: int
    next_escalation_at: str | None
    decision_by: str | None = None
    decision_at: str | None = None

    def spoken(self) -> str:
        """The text a phone call reads out: short, no IDs that are hard to say."""
        text = f"{self.title}. {self.message}"
        if self.action:
            text += f" Proposed action: {self.action}"
        return text


def classify(severity: str, deadline: str | None, impact: str, critical_hours: float,
             now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """
    Derive the severity: never lower than what the producer said, raised to critical when the
    launch is affected and less than `critical_hours` are left before the deadline.
    """
    severity = severity if severity in SEVERITIES else "medium"
    if impact == "launch" and deadline:
        now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
        left = datetime.fromisoformat(deadline) - now
        if left <= timedelta(hours=critical_hours):
            return "critical"
        if left <= timedelta(hours=critical_hours * 3) and SEVERITIES.index(severity) < SEVERITIES.index("high"):
            return "high"
    return severity


class AlertBook:
    """Alert persistence in the same SQLite database as the version store."""

    def __init__(self, store: Store):
        self.store = store
        self.db = store.db
        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)

    def raise_alert(self, *, title: str, message: str, action: str = "", severity: str = "medium",
                    deadline: str | None = None, impact: str = "launch", external: bool = False,
                    source: str = "manual", policy: Policy) -> Alert:
        level = classify(severity, deadline, impact, policy.critical_hours)
        aid = self.db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO alerts (created_at, source, severity, title, message, action, deadline, impact,"
            " external, status, token, chain_index) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'open', ?, 0)",
            (now_iso(), source, level, title, message, action, deadline, impact, int(external),
             secrets.token_urlsafe(16)),
        ).lastrowid
        self.db.commit()
        return self.get(aid)

    def get(self, alert_id: int) -> Alert | None:
        row = self.db.execute("SELECT * FROM alerts WHERE id = ?", (alert_id,)).fetchone()
        if not row:
            return None
        d = dict(row)
        d["external"] = bool(d["external"])
        return Alert(**d)

    def list(self, open_only: bool = False) -> list[Alert]:
        sql = "SELECT id FROM alerts"
        if open_only:
            sql += " WHERE status IN ('open', 'notified', 'escalated')"
        return [self.get(r["id"]) for r in self.db.execute(sql + " ORDER BY id DESC").fetchall()]

    def log(self, alert_id: int, kind: str, channel: str, contact: str, detail: str) -> None:
        self.db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO alert_events (alert_id, at, kind, channel, contact, detail) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (alert_id, now_iso(), kind, channel, contact, detail),
        )
        self.db.commit()

    def events(self, alert_id: int) -> list[dict]:
        rows = self.db.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM alert_events WHERE alert_id = ? ORDER BY id", (alert_id,)
        ).fetchall()
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]

    def update(self, alert_id: int, **fields) -> None:
        cols = ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in fields)
        self.db.execute(f"UPDATE alerts SET {cols} WHERE id = ?", (*fields.values(), alert_id))
        self.db.commit()

    def decide(self, alert_id: int, decision: str, by: str, channel: str, token: str | None = None) -> Alert:
        alert = self.get(alert_id)
        if alert is None:
            raise KeyError(alert_id)
        if token is not None and not secrets.compare_digest(token, alert.token):
            raise PermissionError("invalid alert token")
        if decision not in DECISIONS:
            raise ValueError(f"decision must be one of {', '.join(DECISIONS)}")
        status = DECISIONS[decision]
        fields = {"status": status, "decision_by": by, "decision_at": now_iso()}
        if decision == "escalate":
            fields["chain_index"] = alert.chain_index + 1
            fields["next_escalation_at"] = now_iso()  # escalate right away
        else:
            fields["next_escalation_at"] = None
        self.update(alert_id, **fields)
        self.log(alert_id, "decision", channel, by, decision)
        return self.get(alert_id)

    def as_dict(self, alert: Alert) -> dict:
        d = asdict(alert)
        d.pop("token")
        return d

from ask_soony.store import Store

NOW = datetime(2026, 1, 10, 12, 0, tzinfo=UTC)


def policy() -> Policy:
    return Policy(
        dashboard_url="https://dash.example.com",
        contacts=[
            Contact("buyer", "Alex Buyer", "buyer", phone="[REDACTED_PHONE]", email="[REDACTED_EMAIL]"),
            Contact("head", "Sam Head", "head_of_procurement", phone="[REDACTED_PHONE]"),
        ],
        routes={
            "critical": {"channels": ["dashboard", "call"], "chain": ["buyer", "head"], "ack_minutes": 10},
            "high": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": ["buyer"], "ack_minutes": 0},
            "medium": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": ["buyer"], "ack_minutes": 0},
            "low": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 0},
            "info": {"channels": ["dashboard"], "chain": [], "ack_minutes": 0},
        },

def test_classify_raises_severity_close_to_a_launch_deadline():
    soon = (NOW + timedelta(hours=6)).isoformat()
    later = (NOW + timedelta(hours=48)).isoformat()
    assert classify("medium", soon, "launch", 24, now=NOW) == "critical"
    assert classify("medium", later, "launch", 24, now=NOW) == "high"
    assert classify("medium", soon, "cost", 24, now=NOW) == "medium"
    assert classify("high", None, "launch", 24, now=NOW) == "high"


def test_critical_alert_calls_chain_and_escalates_on_timeout(tmp_path):
    book = AlertBook(Store(tmp_path))
    pol = policy()
    esc = Escalator(book, pol, DryRunCaller(), Mailer("", "", "", dry_run=True))
    alert = book.raise_alert(title="Part short", message="5,900 missing", action="Order 8,000",
                             severity="critical", policy=pol)
    esc.notify(alert)
    calls = [e for e in book.events(alert.id) if e["kind"] == "call"]
    assert calls and calls[0]["contact"] == "buyer"

    late = datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(minutes=11)
    assert esc.tick(now=late) == 1
    calls = [e for e in book.events(alert.id) if e["kind"] == "call"]
    assert [c["contact"] for c in calls] == ["buyer", "head"]

    book.decide(alert.id, "approve", by="head", channel="call")
    assert esc.tick(now=late + timedelta(hours=1)) == 0
    assert book.get(alert.id).status == "approved"

def _post(url: str, data: bytes, ctype: str, auth: str | None = None) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method="POST", headers={"Content-Type": ctype})
    if auth:
        req.add_header("Authorization", "Basic " + base64.b64encode(f"x:{auth}".encode()).decode())
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return resp.status, resp.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        return e.code, e.read()


def test_webhooks_record_decisions_only_with_the_right_token(tmp_path):
    book = AlertBook(Store(tmp_path))
    a1 = book.raise_alert(title="T1", message="M", severity="critical", policy=policy())
    a2 = book.raise_alert(title="T2", message="M", severity="critical", policy=policy())
    server = Dashboard(tmp_path, password="pw").serve(port=0)
    threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
    base = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_port}"
    try:
        code, _ = _post(f"{base}/hooks/twilio/{a1.id}?token=wrong", b"Digits=1", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded")

        assert code == 401
    finally:
        server.shutdown()
    book = AlertBook(Store(tmp_path))
    assert book.get(a1.id).status == "approved"
    assert book.get(a2.id).status == "escalated"

The call notification part is built and runs end to end, still in dry-run mode (no calls, no costs). It's on the new branch `jonas/alerts`.

**How it works:**
1. **Other modules raise alerts**, e.g. verification or prediction: `ask-soony alert raise` or in Python `AlertBook.raise_alert(...)`, with title, message, proposed action, severity, deadline and whether it goes to a supplier.
2. **Criticality is automatic:** near a launch deadline (default under 24 h) an alert becomes "critical", under 72 h at least "high". So the art book case turned critical on its own.
3. **The escalation policy** (`data/alert-policy.json`, gitignored because of phone numbers; example in `docs/`) sets per severity which channels are used, who comes in what order, and how many minutes each person has.
4. **Channels:**
   - dashboard (`/alerts` with Approve / Escalate / Reject),
   - email (only with `ASK_ALERT_EMAIL=on`),
   - call: dry run, **Twilio** (reads the alert aloud, "press 1 to approve, 2 to escalate, 3 to reject") or the **ElevenLabs voice agent** (talks freely, records the decision through a tool).
5. **Decisions come back** through dashboard buttons or call webhooks (secured with a secret per alert). **Nobody answers → the next person**; the `serve` service checks every 30 s.

**Checked:** 13 of 13 tests and lint pass. Live through the tunnel:
- wrong token → rejected;
- keypad "2" → "escalate" recorded;
- within 30 s the next person (Head of Procurement) was notified automatically.

**One thing went wrong:** the first test sent a real email to the placeholder `[REDACTED_EMAIL]`, because the Gmail credentials are set. The address doesn't exist, so only a bounce comes back. Alert emails are now off by default.

**For real calls, you need to:**
1. **Create a Twilio account and buy a number.** This is needed for ElevenLabs too, because ElevenLabs calls through an imported Twilio number. Then put `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` and `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER` in `.env`. With a trial account you can only call verified numbers.
2. **Put your team's phone numbers** in `data/alert-policy.json` (local only).
3. **Set `ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=twilio`** and I'll test a real call to your phone. **For ElevenLabs:** create an agent in their dashboard (prompt and tool are in the README), import the Twilio number, then fill `ELEVENLABS_*` and set the provider to `elevenlabs`.

**For the team:** the others' modules may not be in Python. If so, I could add a small HTTP endpoint (`POST /api/alerts`) so they can raise alerts from anywhere.

**Git:** `jonas/alerts` has 2 new local commits (the supplier status format spec and alerts) on top of the pushed `jonas/watcher-dashboard`. **Not pushed.**

"""
One-off setup for alert calls, run from the repo root:
  uv run python <this file> twilio      buy a US voice number, write TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER, put the
                                        verified mobile into data/alert-policy.json
  uv run python <this file> elevenlabs  create the decision tool and agent, import the Twilio
                                        number, write ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID / _PHONE_NUMBER_ID
Never prints keys or full phone numbers.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import httpx

from ask_soony.config import load_dotenv

load_dotenv()
ENV = Path(".env")
POLICY = Path("data/alert-policy.json")


def mask(number: str) -> str:
    return number[:3] + "…" + number[-2:] if number else "?"


def set_env(key: str, value: str) -> None:
    lines = ENV.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.startswith(f"{key}="):
            lines[i] = f"{key}={value}"
            break
    else:
        lines.append(f"{key}={value}")
    ENV.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    os.environ[key] = value


def twilio() -> None:
    sid, token = os.environ["TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"], os.environ["TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"]
    base = f"https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/{sid}"
    http = httpx.Client(auth=(sid, token), timeout=30)
    acct = http.get(f"{base}.json")
    acct.raise_for_status()
    print("account:", acct.json().get("type"), acct.json().get("status"))

    owned = http.get(f"{base}/IncomingPhoneNumbers.json").json().get("incoming_phone_numbers", [])
    voice = [n for n in owned if n.get("capabilities", {}).get("voice")]
    if voice:
        number = voice[0]["phone_number"]
        print("already own a voice number:", mask(number))
    else:
        found = http.get(
            f"{base}/AvailablePhoneNumbers/US/Local.json", params={"VoiceEnabled": "true", "PageSize": 5}
        ).json().get("available_phone_numbers", [])
        if not found:
            sys.exit("no US voice numbers offered")
        bought = http.post(f"{base}/IncomingPhoneNumbers.json", data={"PhoneNumber": found[0]["phone_number"],
                                                                       "FriendlyName": "ask-soony alerts"})
        if bought.status_code >= 300:
            sys.exit(f"buying failed: HTTP {bought.status_code} {bought.text[:300]}")
        number = bought.json()["phone_number"]
        print("bought:", mask(number))
    set_env("TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER", number)

    verified = http.get(f"{base}/OutgoingCallerIds.json").json().get("outgoing_caller_ids", [])
    print("verified numbers:", [mask(v["phone_number"]) for v in verified])
    if verified and POLICY.exists():
        policy = json.loads(POLICY.read_text())
        for c in policy.get("contacts", []):
            if c["id"] == "buyer":
                c["phone"] = verified[0]["phone_number"]
                c["name"] = "Jonas (as Senior Buyer)"
        POLICY.write_text(json.dumps(policy, indent=2))
        print("policy: buyer phone set to", mask(verified[0]["phone_number"]))


PROMPT = """You are the procurement alert assistant of Soony Interactive. You call a person because \
something threatens the product launch and a decision is needed now.

The person you are calling: {{contact_name}}.
Alert: {{alert_title}}.
Details: {{alert_message}}
Proposed action: {{proposed_action}}
Deadline: {{deadline}}

Explain the problem in two or three short sentences, then the proposed action. Answer questions \
briefly with the facts above; do not invent numbers. Then ask for a decision: approve the action, \
escalate to the next person, or reject. As soon as the person decides, call the tool \
record_decision with the decision, confirm it in one sentence and end the call politely. If the \
person cannot decide now, record "escalate"."""


def elevenlabs() -> None:
    key = os.environ["ELEVENLABS_API_KEY"]
    public = os.environ.get("ASK_PUBLIC_URL", "").rstrip("/")
    if not public:
        sys.exit("ASK_PUBLIC_URL missing")
    http = httpx.Client(base_url="https://api.elevenlabs.io", headers={"xi-api-key": key}, timeout=60)

    tool = http.post("/v1/convai/tools", json={"tool_config": {
        "type": "webhook",
        "name": "record_decision",
        "description": "Record the person's decision on the alert: approve, escalate or reject.",
        "api_schema": {
            "url": f"{public}/hooks/elevenlabs/decision",
            "method": "POST",
            "content_type": "application/json",
            "request_body_schema": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                    "alert_id": {"type": "string", "dynamic_variable": "alert_id"},
                    "token": {"type": "string", "dynamic_variable": "secret__alert_token"},
                    "decision": {"type": "string", "enum": ["approve", "escalate", "reject"],
                                 "description": "The decision the person made"},
                },
                "required": ["alert_id", "token", "decision"],
            },
        },
    }})
    if tool.status_code >= 300:
        sys.exit(f"tool failed: HTTP {tool.status_code} {tool.text[:400]}")
    tool_id = tool.json()["id"]
    print("tool created")

    agent = http.post("/v1/convai/agents/create", json={
        "name": "ask-soony alert caller",
        "conversation_config": {"agent": {
            "first_message": "Hello {{contact_name}}, this is the Soony procurement assistant with an "
                             "urgent launch alert: {{alert_title}}. Do you have a minute?",
            "language": "en",
            "prompt": {"prompt": PROMPT, "tool_ids": [tool_id]},
        }},
    })
    if agent.status_code >= 300:
        sys.exit(f"agent failed: HTTP {agent.status_code} {agent.text[:400]}")
    agent_id = agent.json()["agent_id"]
    set_env("ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID", agent_id)
    print("agent created")

    number = os.environ["TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER"]
    imported = http.post("/v1/convai/phone-numbers", json={
        "provider": "twilio", "label": "ask-soony alerts", "phone_number": number,
        "sid": os.environ["TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"], "token": os.environ["TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"],
        "agent_id": agent_id,
    })
    if imported.status_code >= 300:
        sys.exit(f"phone import failed: HTTP {imported.status_code} {imported.text[:400]}")
    set_env("ELEVENLABS_PHONE_NUMBER_ID", imported.json()["phone_number_id"])
    print("number imported and assigned to the agent")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"twilio": twilio, "elevenlabs": elevenlabs}[sys.argv[1]]()

content.text:
You're right, and that changes things. **The Twilio trial has changed.** According to this page (and the general trials page):
- **Trial accounts no longer buy numbers.** They call from a **shared Twilio trial number** (*"shared Twilio-owned numbers"*). That's why buying failed.
- **Your signup number counts as verified automatically.** Up to 5 numbers can be verified.
- **Limits:** 75 free call minutes, max 10 minutes per call, only to verified numbers, **only within your signup country**.
- **Allowed:** text-to-speech and **keypad input**, so exactly our "press 1 to approve" version.
- **Blocked:** `<Stream>`, `<Dial>`, `<Record>`.

**What that means for us:**
- **The Twilio keypad call should work for free on the trial.** That's enough for the demo: the phone rings, reads the alert, you press 1, and the dashboard shows "approved".
- **The ElevenLabs voice agent doesn't work on the trial,** because it needs a number of its own to import (and the media stream). That would need the upgrade.

The only thing I'm missing is **which trial number** the calls come from. As far as I can tell from the docs, Twilio only shows it in the console:

1. In the Twilio console: **Communications → Voice → Overview → "Try out Voice"**.
2. On "Start a call" a **From number** appears, the trial number. Optionally make the test call there once; it shows the number works for you.
3. Put that number in `.env`:
   ```
   TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER=+...
   ```
4. Write **"from is in"**.

Then I'll start our first real alert call to your mobile (art book alert, keypad), with no upgrade and no costs. If the API rejects our own call text on the trial, we'll see it from the error message, and the fallback would be Twilio's own keypad template from the docs.

Are there any alternatives that allows free calls or have a student program?

Yes, and the best one you already have: **the new Twilio trial is free for our case.** 75 call minutes, no card, keypad input allowed. All that's missing is the trial number from the console. That makes it the simplest free option.

The alternatives, as far as I know them (I haven't checked current terms, and those can change):

| Provider | Free part | Catch |
|---|---|---|
| **Twilio trial** (yours) | 75 min, shared trial number, keypad calls | Only verified numbers, only within your signup country, **no ElevenLabs agent** |
| **Vonage (Voice API)** | Small starting credit | Test numbers must be registered, often a number to buy too |
| **Plivo** | Trial credit | Only verified "sandbox" numbers |
| **Sinch, Infobip** | Free trial with test calls to your own number | Sign-up with business details, sometimes manual approval |
| **Telnyx** | Cheap; credit after verification | Usually wants a card or deposit for numbers |
| **Azure Communication Services** (Azure for Students $100) | Student credit | As far as I know, **phone numbers aren't available on student or trial subscriptions**. Unconfirmed |

**Student programs:** I know of none that currently gives free phone credit. Twilio is no longer in the GitHub Student Pack.

**Completely free without the phone network:**
- **Telegram bot** with an ElevenLabs voice message plus Approve/Escalate buttons,
- **browser call** to the ElevenLabs agent on the dashboard.

Both work reliably, just without "a phone ringing".

**My recommendation:**
1. **Now:** get the trial "From" number from Twilio's "Try out Voice" page and put it in `.env`. Then the keypad call runs for free, and that's our demo call.
2. **If you want the talking ElevenLabs agent on the phone:** ask on the Discord or at a sponsor booth for a Twilio promo code (upgrade at no cost), or pay the upgrade (probably about $20). Without it, the voice agent can run in the browser for free.

content.text:
**Azure is out, unfortunately.** Microsoft's docs are explicit: *"You can't acquire phone numbers using Azure free credits."* Phone numbers need a paid pay-as-you-go subscription, and credits can't be used for them. Azure's free trial number would exist, but only calls verified **US numbers (+1)**, so it can't reach your German mobile. Your $180 doesn't help here.

**Voice-to-voice or keypad?** I wouldn't make the voice model a must. There are two different things:

| | Text-to-speech + keypad | Voice-to-voice agent (ElevenLabs / GPT-Realtime) |
|---|---|---|
| What happens | The call reads the alert, "press 1 to approve, 2 to escalate" | The agent talks freely; you can ask "What does it cost? Is there an alternative?" and decide by voice |
| Reliability | Very high: a keypress is unambiguous | Medium: noise in the hall, misunderstandings, latency |
| Fit with the interviews | Felix: decision at the right moment, auditable | Nice for "the system explains itself", but the decision has to be recorded cleanly anyway |
| Cost / requirement | **Free on the Twilio trial** | Needs a Twilio number of your own, so the upgrade, or a browser call |
| Wow effect on stage | Good: a phone rings and the dashboard turns green | Very good, if it works live |

**My recommendation:**
1. **The phone call in the demo stays text-to-speech plus keypad.** It's free, robust, and the decision lands unambiguously on the dashboard. You don't need a transcript: the keypress *is* the record.
2. **The talking agent comes on top as an option:** either in the **browser** (free, with your ElevenLabs credits, e.g. "ask the agent about the alert") or later on the phone, if a promo code or upgrade comes along. In the pitch it's enough to say: "for difficult cases the voice agent explains and answers questions". The code is already there.

So the next step stays the same: the trial "From" number from Twilio's "Try out Voice" page into `.env` as `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER`, and I'll start the first free test call to your mobile.

"pay-as-you-go subscription" I think I have this? how to try it? do they have some api / mcp. So far I have no resource group [Image #10]
[Image: source: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jonasstenglein-OtherProjects-StartMunichHack-ask-soony/3021cc1a-f777-4712-b18b-d31b6ece5ff1/images/10.png]

Pay-as-you-go helps less than it sounds:
- **The $180 credit can't be used for phone numbers or calls.** Microsoft writes that prepaid credits are "not eligible" for them. Even on pay-as-you-go, the number and the call minutes go **onto your card**. That's only a few dollars, but not free.
- **Setup takes more steps than Twilio:**
  1. create the ACS resource (your screenshot),
  2. buy a number, and with European billing it's unclear which country's numbers are allowed (German numbers usually need address documents),
  3. create an Azure AI services resource and connect it to ACS with a managed identity, because text-to-speech and keypad recognition depend on it,
  4. build our code in, in a new format: an event callback instead of a single API call.
- **Realistically 1.5–2 hours,** with uncertainties at the number purchase. Everything works through the Azure CLI (`az communication …`) and the Python SDK; I'd need to see whether `az` is installed here.

**Comparison for tonight:**

| | Twilio trial (yours) | Azure ACS |
|---|---|---|
| Cost | **Free** (75 min) | A few $ on the card |
| Missing piece | **One value:** the From number from "Try out Voice" | Resource, number, AI services, code adapter |
| Time | **~5 min** to the first call | ~1.5–2 h |
| Voice agent (ElevenLabs) | Only with upgrade | Not directly (ElevenLabs only takes Twilio/SIP) |

**My clear recommendation: you don't need to fill in the Azure form.** Cancel it and take the Twilio trial path. The only thing missing is the From number:

1. Twilio console → **Communications → Voice → Overview → "Try out Voice"**,
2. copy the trial number shown under **From** into `.env` as `TWILIO_FROM_NUMBER=+...`,
3. write **"from is in"**, and your phone rings with the art book alert.

Keep Azure as a fallback, if the Twilio trial unexpectedly blocks our own call text.

The alert call works: **your phone rang, read the art book alert, you pressed 1, and the dashboard shows "approved". Free, on the Twilio trial.**

**What was needed for the trial:**
- The trial **blocks the call text inside the API request**. So Twilio now fetches the script (text plus "press 1/2/3") from our server through the tunnel (`/hooks/twilio/twiml/<alert>`), protected by the secret token per alert.
- Calls come from Twilio's shared trial number (`+49 158…`), which was in your code snippet.
- Twilio status: **completed, 39 s**. The keypress went through the webhook straight into the decision log.

**Also fixed:**
- **Phone numbers are masked** in the decision log (only the last 2 digits), including the entries already stored. The full number had shown up once in my tool output.
- The README documents the trial setup.

**Checks:** 13 of 13 tests pass, lint clean. The service runs again with the new code.

**The trial's limits:**
- Calls go only to **verified numbers in Germany** (up to 5). For the demo, have teammates verify their numbers in the Twilio console on the "Try out Voice" page (SMS code), then add their numbers to `data/alert-policy.json`.
- **75 free minutes,** at most 10 minutes per call.
- **The ElevenLabs voice agent isn't possible on the trial** (no number of our own). Free alternative: in the browser.

**Still open, your decision:**
1. **Real calls for everything automatic?** Right now only my test command calls for real. The running service (escalations every 30 s) stays in dry run until you set `ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=twilio` in `.env`. My suggestion: switch it on, since only critical alerts call.
2. **Push?** `jonas/alerts` has 3 local commits (status format spec, alerts, trial fix) on top of the pushed `jonas/watcher-dashboard`.

result: First real alert call works on the free Twilio trial (39 s call, keypad "1" recorded as "approved" on the dashboard); committed on `jonas/alerts` (3 commits, not pushed). Teammates need to verify their numbers to be called, and the ElevenLabs voice agent needs a Twilio upgrade.
The voice is not really natural though. What did you use? And we want voice input / natural conversation

I used Twilio's **standard `<Say>` voice**, Twilio's free built-in text-to-speech, which sounds robotic. There are two ways to get a natural voice and voice input:

**A. Stay on the free trial, turn by turn:**
- **Natural voice:** your ElevenLabs credits generate the audio for each sentence, and Twilio plays it with `<Play>`. So the ElevenLabs voice, but no live streaming.
- **Voice input:** Twilio's `<Gather input="speech">` turns your answer into text (about $0.02 per recognition). The trial explicitly offers speech recognition as a template.
- **Understanding:** an LLM interprets the answer ("yes, order", "how much is it?", "ask Maren") and either answers or records the decision. It needs an LLM key: OpenAI (you have credits from the sponsor) or Claude.
- **Feel:** like a real phone conversation, but **1–3 seconds pause per turn**, and no interrupting.
- **Effort:** about 1–1.5 h. Free apart from a few cents. Risk: I haven't tested whether the trial allows `<Play>` and speech input in our own script. That shows on the first try.

**B. Twilio upgrade (about $20) → ElevenLabs voice agent, as originally planned:**
- **Real live conversation:** natural voice, interruptions possible, short latency, questions answered freely, decision recorded through the tool.
- **Effort: about 15 minutes**, because the code and setup script are ready (buy number, create agent, import number).
- Cost: $20 credit, of which the demo uses realistically under $5.

**Comparison:**

| | A: trial, turn by turn | B: upgrade + ElevenLabs agent |
|---|---|---|
| Voice | ElevenLabs (natural) | ElevenLabs (natural) |
| Conversation | Turn by turn, with pauses | **Live, interruptible** |
| Cost | ~0 € | ~$20 credit |
| Time to working | 1–1.5 h | **~15 min** |
| Risk tonight | Medium (trial limits) | Low |

**My recommendation: B,** if the $20 is OK for you, or if someone on the Discord or at a booth has a Twilio code. It's the better demo for much less work, and it's exactly what was planned in the sync ("phone call via ElevenLabs"). **A** is the free fallback. How long would credits be valid?

I haven't been able to confirm that from Twilio's docs, but as far as I know:
- **Twilio credit doesn't expire.** It stays in the account as long as the account exists. Your upgrade page also says "Refreshed free units with **no 30 day limit**". Only the trial is time-limited, not the paid balance.
- **What eats the credit over time is the phone number:** about **$1.15 per month** for a US number, as long as you keep it. Calls are only charged when they happen.
- **Things to watch:**
  1. When upgrading, **leave "auto recharge" off**, so no more money is charged automatically.
  2. **After the hackathon, release the number** (Phone Numbers → Manage → the number → Release). Then nothing is charged anymore, and the rest of the credit stays.
  3. Accounts unused for a very long time can be closed by Twilio; then any leftover credit is probably gone. That's not a problem for a few months.

- demo and tests realistically $2–5 in calls (US number to German mobiles about $0.38 per minute, ElevenLabs minutes from your credits),

I checked. Twilio's official pages don't settle it fully:

**Confirmed:**
- **Not refundable:** Twilio's Terms of Service (as of 16 Jul 2026, §3.3) say paid fees are *"non-refundable"*, apart from exceptions such as Twilio terminating or a service failure. So **the $20 won't come back**, only stay usable as credit.
- **Number cost:** **$1.15 per month** for a US number (toll-free $2.15), as long as you keep it. Optional emergency calling $0.75/month, which we don't need.

**Not confirmed** (no statement in the terms or pricing pages; Twilio's help center can't be read automatically, only in a browser):
- **whether the credit expires** or an inactive account gets closed. I found no expiry or inactivity clause in the terms. Closing is only mentioned for breaches of contract.
- **the minimum upgrade amount** ($20 is the usual figure, but not documented anywhere I could read).
- **whether auto-recharge is on by default.**

**For safety, when upgrading:**
1. In the upgrade dialog, **note the shown minimum amount and any auto-recharge option, and switch auto-recharge off.**
2. Afterwards, under **Billing** in the console, check that auto-recharge is off.
3. After the hackathon, **release the number**, so the $1.15 per month stops.

**My assessment:** worst case, you spend $20 that never comes back, and the rest of the credit sits in the account unused. Expected use tonight is $2–5. Every route needs a number plus a media stream to the voice model, and the providers only unlock that with credit. That explains the error. **Twilio only offers German local and mobile numbers to businesses, not to private individuals:**

| German number | Individual | Business |
|---|---|---|
| Local | **not offered** | yes (business documents needed) |
| Mobile | **not offered** | yes (business documents needed) |
| Toll-free (0800) | yes | yes |

You probably chose "Individual" in the console, and for "Germany Local, Individual" there are no rules at all, hence "Regulation not found".

**What's left:**
- **Business bundle:** needs company documents, such as a trade registration or commercial register extract. Without a company, not an option.
- **German toll-free number (0800) as an individual:** exists, but as far as I know toll-free numbers at Twilio are meant for receiving calls and aren't suited as the caller for outbound calls (not confirmed). They're also more expensive per month. I wouldn't pursue it.

**So the US number stays.** It works, costs $0.38 per minute to German mobiles, and the hackathon budget is a few dollars. You can stop the bundle in the console; nothing has been charged for it.

content.text:
Yes, OpenAI supports it natively. GPT-Realtime has a **SIP phone interface**: phone calls go straight to OpenAI's model, with no audio relay server of our own. There are two variants:

| Variant | How | For us |
|---|---|---|
| **OpenAI dials out itself** (newer "GPT-Live" API) | One API call with the number, and OpenAI calls through a SIP trunk | Needs a SIP trunk with encrypted media (TLS + SRTP). Unclear whether Twilio supports that here (not confirmed) |
| **Twilio calls, then hands over to OpenAI** | Our Twilio number calls your phone. When you answer, Twilio forwards the call to `sip:<project>@sip.api.openai.com`. OpenAI notifies our server by webhook, and we accept the call with the alert text as instructions | **Works with what we have**: Twilio number, tunnel, webhook endpoint. About 1–1.5 h of code |

**Variant 2 in detail:**
1. Alert is critical → Twilio calls your phone (our existing code).
2. On answering, our script tells Twilio to forward the call to OpenAI.
3. OpenAI sends our server the event `realtime.call.incoming`. We **accept** with model `gpt-realtime-2.1`, a voice, instructions (the alert text), and a **`record_decision` function**.
4. A second connection (WebSocket) lets our server see when the model calls the function, record the decision on the dashboard, and end the call.

**Cost:** GPT-Realtime is billed by audio tokens (from the sponsor credits). The Twilio-to-OpenAI SIP hop costs $0.004/min, plus the Twilio leg to your phone ($0.38/min from the US number).

**What I need from you (OpenAI dashboard, same project):**
1. **API key:** `OPENAI_API_KEY=REDACTED in `.env`.
2. **Project ID** (`proj_...`, under Settings → Project → General): `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID=...` in `.env`.
3. **Webhook:** Settings → Project → Webhooks → create endpoint
   - URL: `https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev/hooks/openai`
   - event: **`realtime.call.incoming`**
   - copy the signing secret (`whsec_...`, shown only once) into `.env` as `OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET=REDACTED

Meanwhile I'll build the OpenAI call provider: the handover script, webhook check, accepting the call, function handling, and tests. The ElevenLabs agent stays as an alternative; both sit behind the same interface (`ASK_CALL_PROVIDER=openai` or `elevenlabs`).

needs input: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` and the webhook (`realtime.call.incoming` → `/hooks/openai`, secret as `OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) in `.env`/the OpenAI dashboard; then write "openai is in".
why not option 1?

Option 1 is the nicer one: OpenAI dials itself, and we wouldn't need the handover or the webhook. I didn't pick it because of three uncertainties:

1. **The SIP trunk:** OpenAI requires **TLS plus encrypted media (SRTP)** from the trunk. Twilio has a product for this ("Elastic SIP Trunking" with secure trunking), but I couldn't confirm it works with OpenAI's requirements, and it means extra setup (trunk, credentials, termination address).
2. **The decision tool:** in the newer "GPT-Live" API, OpenAI hasn't documented how our own tools (like `record_decision`) are called in this mode. For the older Realtime API used in option 2, the tool flow is well known.
3. **Newness:** GPT-Live is the newer API generation, with fewer examples and more risk of hitting something undocumented tonight. Option 2 has an official Twilio + OpenAI Realtime tutorial behind it, even if only for incoming calls.

| | Option 1: OpenAI dials | Option 2: Twilio hands over |
|---|---|---|
| Running logic | Simpler (one API call) | A little more (webhook + accept) |
| Setup | SIP trunk with TLS/SRTP at Twilio (not confirmed) | Only the webhook in the OpenAI dashboard |
| Decision tool | Not documented for this mode | Documented |
| Risk tonight | **Higher** | **Lower** |

**Suggestion:** I'll **try option 1 with a time limit of 30 minutes**: create a Twilio SIP trunk with encryption by API, then a test call through OpenAI. If it works, it's the cleaner solution. If it hits a wall (trunk, encryption, tool), I'll switch to option 2. Both use the same OpenAI key and project. Option 1 needs **no webhook**; option 2 does.

So for now I only need `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` in `.env`. Set up the webhook only if we need option 2. Write "openai is in" when the two values are there.

"2. The decision tool: in the newer "GPT-Live" API, OpenAI hasn't documented how our own tools (like record_decision) are called in this mode. For the older Realtime API used in option 2, the tool flow is well known." why not gpt-realtime but gpt-live?

Because of where each feature lives in OpenAI's API:

- **"OpenAI dials out itself" only exists in the new GPT-Live API.** The call is created with `POST /v1/live/sessions` and a SIP target. **GPT-Realtime** (`gpt-realtime-2.1`) has no outbound calls; it can only **accept** incoming SIP calls.
- That means:
  - **GPT-Realtime only works with option 2:** Twilio calls your phone and hands the call to OpenAI as an "incoming" call, which we accept.
  - **Option 1 automatically means GPT-Live** (`gpt-live-1`), and with it the undocumented tool handling.

| | GPT-Realtime (`gpt-realtime-2.1`) | GPT-Live (`gpt-live-1`) |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI dials itself | no | **yes** |
| Calls via Twilio handover | **yes** (option 2) | yes |
| Own tools (decision) | **documented** (function calls) | not clearly documented for this mode |
| Price | per audio token ($32/$64 per 1M) | **$0.05/min** (active), simpler |

**My recommendation stays:** **GPT-Realtime via option 2.** It's the documented path, with reliable decision recording through a function call. Option 1 / GPT-Live would be more elegant, but carries two uncertainties at once (SIP trunk with encryption, plus the tool handling).

So, for option 2 I need:
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `OPENAI_PROJECT_ID` (`proj_...`)
- the **webhook** in the OpenAI dashboard: event `realtime.call.incoming` → `https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev/hooks/openai`, with the secret as `OPENAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in `.env`.

Write "openai is in" when those are there. Meanwhile I'll start writing the code.

"  - GPT-Realtime only works with option 2: Twilio calls your phone and hands the call to OpenAI as an "incoming" call, which we accept." how much delay is this?

Mainly **once at the start of the call**, barely in the conversation itself. My estimates, not measured:

**When answering (once):**
1. You answer → Twilio fetches our call script through the tunnel: about **0.2–0.5 s**
2. Twilio forwards the call to OpenAI (SIP): about **0.2–0.5 s**
3. OpenAI notifies our server (webhook) → we accept with the alert text: about **0.3–0.8 s**
4. The model generates its greeting: about **0.5–1 s**

→ **About 1.5–3 seconds of silence** after answering before the agent speaks. We can cover that with a short Twilio announcement ("Connecting you to the Soony procurement assistant…"), so it doesn't feel like a dead line.

**During the conversation (every turn):**
- The audio flows **directly** from Twilio to OpenAI, without detours through our server, and without transcription in between: GPT-Realtime hears and speaks itself.
- The delay is therefore roughly the model's normal response time (often around **0.5–1 s**), plus a little network delay. Twilio's media runs through the US by default, OpenAI's SIP too. We can move both to Europe (Twilio region `de1`/`ie1`, OpenAI `sip-eu.api.openai.com`), which saves another ~100–200 ms.
- **Our server is only involved** when the model records the decision (function call), and that runs in parallel to speaking.

**Compared with the other variants:**
- **ElevenLabs agent:** similar start delay (ElevenLabs connects through Twilio too), similar conversation latency.
- **OpenAI dials itself (option 1):** saves at most the ~0.5 s of the handover at the start.

**So:** about 2 s at the start (which we can mask), and in the conversation it feels like a normal voice assistant. We'll see the actual figures on the first test call, and I can measure the times in the log.

content.text:
Yes, a voice conversation **in the browser** is the cheapest way to test, with no Twilio costs at all:

| Option | Cost | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Browser / web app voice call** (GPT-Realtime via WebRTC) | **Only OpenAI tokens, no Twilio** | **Recommended.** A "Talk about this alert" button on the alert page. Works on laptop and **phone browser** (through our HTTPS tunnel). Same instructions, same voice, same `record_decision` → dashboard. The browser also brings **its own echo and noise suppression** |
| Telegram | Free | **Bots can't make calls.** Only voice messages back and forth, no live conversation |
| SIP app on the phone (e.g. Linphone) via Twilio | ~$0.004/min instead of $0.38 | Rings in an app, but setup (SIP domain, credentials) is more involved |
| OpenAI Playground | Tokens | Only for tuning the prompt, not our flow |

**How the browser variant would work:**
1. You open an alert on the dashboard and click **"Talk to the assistant"**.
2. Our server fetches a **short-lived key** from OpenAI (your API key never reaches the browser) with exactly the same session settings as on the phone.
3. The browser connects directly to GPT-Realtime (WebRTC). You talk through the microphone, it answers through the speaker.
4. When you decide, the model calls `record_decision`, the browser sends it to our server (secured by the alert's token), and the alert turns green.

**Benefit:** you can test as often as you like for cents, tune prompt and noise behaviour, and it doubles as the "app" variant for the demo or a PWA later. The **phone call** stays for the real escalation moment.

**Effort:** about 45–60 minutes. Should I build it?

Meanwhile, if you want to test the phone call once more with the new noise filter: turn on **Voice Isolation** on your iPhone (Control Center → Mic Mode during a call). Just say "call".
